title: Musk Reportedly Sought Intel, TSMC and Micron Plants Before Terafab Push
gist: Per The Elec, Elon Musk reportedly tried and failed to buy chip plants from Intel, TSMC and Micron before pursuing his Terafab project, which targets 100,000 wafers per month before 2030 and eventually one million. Terafab is lining up suppliers including Lam Research and Applied Materials, while Musk and TSMC's C.C. Wei diverge on who would operate any shared plants.

insights.claim: Elon Musk reportedly explored buying semiconductor facilities from Intel, TSMC and Micron before launching Terafab, and after rejection shifted toward partnerships.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Incumbents declined to sell fabs, forcing a build-from-scratch path with partners.

insights.claim: Terafab has reportedly contacted Korean suppliers and American equipment companies including Lam Research and Applied Materials about piping, polishing slurries, cleaning chemicals and other materials.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Potential new demand for WFE and materials vendors if Terafab proceeds.
insights.locator: The report says Terafab has contacted

insights.claim: Suppliers have reportedly been surprised by Terafab's execution speed, with engineers given authority to make decisions quickly, though building advanced fabs remains technically demanding.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Speed could help but fab ramps are historically hard.

insights.claim: Industry observers expect Terafab's initial production target to reach 100,000 wafers per month before 2030, with Musk's eventual ambition at one million wafers monthly for autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots and other ventures.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A million wafers/month would be a step-change in global capacity; treat as aspirational.
insights.locator: Industry observers expect Terafab’s initial production

insights.claim: Musk has said TSMC's maximum involvement would be as a subcontractor, while TSMC CEO C.C. Wei has indicated TSMC would need to operate the plants for a partnership to work.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Control over operations is the sticking point in any Musk-TSMC deal.

insights.claim: The supplied report also describes Intel as a Terafab partner, linking its involvement to its 14A manufacturing technology.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Would be a potential external customer validation for Intel 14A if confirmed.

insights.claim: In a conversation with Walter Isaacson, Musk argued that physical AI could conduct experiments, manufacture goods and enable activity in space, and that robots, lunar infrastructure and space development could eventually support an economy a million times larger than Earth's.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Long-term narrative used to justify massive chip capacity; not near-term investable.

insights.claim: Terafab's immediate challenge is converting supplier discussions, manufacturing partnerships and ambitious targets into a functioning semiconductor operation that delivers chips reliably at scale.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Monitor concrete tool orders and site milestones rather than targets.
